fix.loadErrorPortfolio: Could not load the portfolio. Check your connection and reload the page.
fix.loadErrorTasks: Could not load tasks. Check your connection.
fix.dateOrder: Start cannot be later than finish
fix.importDup: A project with this name already exists. Create a copy anyway?

adopt.baselineWhat: A baseline is a snapshot of the dates you committed to. The project moves on, dates shift — the snapshot stays. At any status meeting you can show: what was promised → what it is now → how many days it slipped and on which tasks.
adopt.baselineStep1: Agree the work plan (WBS) and dates.
adopt.baselineStep2: Freeze it with the button below — all task dates are saved as the baseline.
adopt.baselineStep3: When dates slip, this page shows the deviation per task, and the Gantt shows the baseline as a grey bar under each task.
adopt.ganttAutoShift: Move a task — every dependent task shifts automatically. The thing you used to redraw by hand in Excel.
adopt.wbsBitrix: Assign a person and click Bitrix24 in the task row — the task lands in their Bitrix by itself. They don't need a portal account.
adopt.importHint: Your existing Excel template (charter, WBS, risks…) comes in with one click.
adopt.importWow: {{count}} tasks on the timeline. Move one — the dependent ones shift by themselves.
adopt.sheetsMissing: Sheets not recognized: {{sheets}} — you can add these sections manually.
adopt.loginTagline: A Gantt that shifts itself. Reports that build themselves.
adopt.myWorkEmpty: Your tasks from all projects will gather here. Add tasks to the work plan.
adopt.icsTitle: Deadlines straight into your Outlook/Google calendar

empty.team: Enter people once — then assign tasks in two clicks instead of from memory.
empty.stakeholders: Write down who influences the project — and before every conversation you'll have a cheat sheet: who, about what, how often.
empty.assumptions: Capture agreements and constraints now — in six months you won't have to remember why you decided this way.
empty.commPlan: Write down who you report to and when — meetings and updates stop living in your head.
empty.kpis: 3–5 measurable goals — and you answer “how is the project going?” with numbers, not feelings.
empty.risks: Write down what can go wrong — and a nasty surprise turns into a ready action plan.
empty.decisions: Log decisions with “who and why” — a month later nobody argues about who came up with it.
empty.budget: Add your cost lines — and see plan, actuals, and variance without pivot tables in Excel.
empty.backlog: Drop every idea and request here — nothing gets lost, and the good ones become tasks in one click.
empty.reports: Your first report takes 10 minutes: risks and numbers are pulled from your data, and the board sees the status without calling you.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.hint: The theme applies instantly and is remembered. Light/dark mode is toggled in the bottom-left menu.

auth.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts, please wait a minute

errors.forbidden: You don't have permission for this action
errors.boundaryBody: An unexpected error occurred in the interface. Please reload the page.

project.coEditorsHint: A co-manager (deputy) can edit the project on par with the PM.

fields.name: Name
fields.codeHint: Short project identifier used in reports, portfolio views, and integrations.
fields.versionHint: Current passport version. Increases when important project details are revised.
fields.versionDateHint: Date when the current passport version was recorded.
fields.statusHint: Overall lifecycle state of the project.
fields.nameHint: Official project name used across the portal and reports.
fields.clientHint: Customer, sponsor, or business owner requesting the project.
fields.pmHint: Person accountable for day-to-day project delivery.
fields.priorityHint: How urgent and important this project is for the portfolio.
fields.plannedStartHint: Approved planned start date for the project.
fields.plannedEndHint: Approved planned finish date for the project.
fields.actualEndHint: Actual date the project was completed or closed.
fields.goalHint: The measurable outcome the project must achieve. Be specific and result-oriented.
fields.scopeHint: What is included in (and excluded from) the project. Defines project boundaries.
fields.resultHint: Tangible deliverables produced by the project that stakeholders will receive.
fields.keyMilestonesHint: Major checkpoints or decision gates that mark significant progress points.
fields.pmHintLocked: Use the “Hand over” button in the project header to change the manager. Available to the project's primary manager and to the portfolio manager — the project moves along with the name.
fields.pmHintOnCreate: You become the manager of a new project. You can hand it over right after creating it, with the “Hand over” button in the project header.

list.title: Projects
list.summary_one: {{count}} project is currently visible in the workspace.
list.summary_other: {{count}} projects are currently visible in the workspace.
list.emptyStateDescription: Create the first project passport to start planning, communication, and portfolio tracking.

project.deleteConfirm: Delete project "%s"? This cannot be undone.
project.saveFailed: Failed to save. Please try again.
project.notFound: Project not found or failed to load.
project.createDescription: Create the project foundation first so planning, reporting, and portfolio oversight start from one source of truth.
project.createGuideText: Describe the goal, dates, owner, and expected result first. The rest of the project workspace will build on this foundation.
project.guidedNavigationDesc: Sections are grouped by purpose so new users can move from setup to planning and control.
project.launchChecklistDesc: A simple sequence for users who do not yet know standard PM terminology.
project.setupDescription: A lightweight view of what is already captured and what still needs attention.
project.startHint: Passport and work plan are enough to start. Add the rest later.
project.createdNext: Passport is ready. Add the first 3–5 tasks — the Gantt, calendar, and report will build themselves from them.

setup.passportNote: Goal, owner, and target end date are defined.
setup.planNote: {{count}} tasks are currently in the work breakdown.
setup.risksNote: {{count}} open risks are tracked right now.

passportGuide.s1d: Fill in the name, status, client, PM, and planned dates; add actual dates as the project runs.
passportGuide.s2d: Describe the goal, scope, results, and key milestones as lists — one item per line.
passportGuide.s3d: Nothing to click: the passport saves itself, and the version updates once per editing session.
passportGuide.s4d: The PDF button opens browser print: choose "Save as PDF" to export the full passport.
passportGuide.s5d: Below are previews of team, risks, KPIs, and more — "Open" and "Add" take you straight there.

passportDefinitions.statusDesc: Planning = being prepared. Active = delivery is underway. On hold = temporarily paused. Completed or Cancelled = closed.
passportDefinitions.priorityDesc: Shows how urgent and important the project is for the portfolio. It is not a status.
passportDefinitions.clientDesc: The person or party requesting the project and expecting the outcome. This is usually the source of business expectations.
passportDefinitions.pmDesc: The person coordinating day-to-day delivery, communication, timeline, and risk handling.

passport.description: Fix the purpose, owner, dates, and expected outcome of the project.
passport.helpText: If someone asks what this project is and why it exists, this section should answer it.

team.description: List who works on the project and what each person is responsible for.
team.helpText: Use project roles, not only job titles, so responsibility is clear during delivery.

stakeholders.description: Track who can influence the project and how actively they need communication.
stakeholders.helpText: This section helps avoid surprises from sponsors, clients, and teams affected by the project.

assumptions.description: Capture conditions that must remain true, plus important limits around time, scope, or resources.
assumptions.helpText: Anything that can invalidate the plan later should be written here early.

commPlan.description: Define what updates are sent, to whom, how often, and by which channel.
commPlan.helpText: Use this to set expectations for weekly check-ins, steering updates, and stakeholder messaging.

kpis.description: Track the metrics that show whether the project is delivering the intended result.
kpis.helpText: A KPI should help you answer whether the project is improving something measurable.

wbs.noviceLabel: What work has to be done
wbs.description: Break the project into phases, tasks, owners, and dates.
wbs.helpText: If work is not in the WBS, it is easy to forget, under-resource, or miss in reporting.

gantt.description: Visualize schedule, dependencies, and overlaps across project tasks.
gantt.helpText: Use the timeline to spot conflicts, bottlenecks, and unrealistic date assumptions.

kanban.description: See tasks grouped by status and move them across columns as work progresses.
kanban.helpText: Drag a card to a new column to update its status without opening the work breakdown.

baseline.description: Freeze an approved version of the plan so later deviations can be measured.
baseline.helpText: A baseline is what you compare current reality against when someone asks what changed.

risks.description: Track threats to delivery, their impact, and how the team will respond.
risks.helpText: A project with no logged risks usually means the team has not looked hard enough yet.

decisions.description: Record important choices, rationale, and implications for the team.
decisions.helpText: Decision logs reduce repeated debates and help newcomers understand past tradeoffs.

budget.description: Plan and track expected spend across the project.
budget.helpText: Budget control is easier when cost lines are visible before spending starts.

backlog.description: Keep a queue of unresolved actions, requests, and ideas that still need ownership.
backlog.helpText: Use the backlog when an item matters but should not yet become part of the committed work plan.

meetings.description: Prepare recurring meetings, capture minutes, and turn discussions into actions.
meetings.helpText: Meeting notes should tell an absent stakeholder what changed and what needs follow-up.

reports.description: Publish periodic project status, RAG signal, milestones, and next steps.
reports.helpText: This is the management view that turns detailed project data into a concise health update.

subprojects.description: Progress, overdue work, risks and budget of every subproject in one table.
subprojects.helpText: Use it when a large programme is split into modules led by different managers.

project.readOnlyHint: View only: editing is available to this project's lead PM.
project.cloneConfirm: Create a copy of the project (passport and structure, without tasks)?
project.archiveConfirm: Archive this project? It will be hidden from the portfolio.
project.forbidden: You do not have access to this project. It belongs to another manager.
project.missing: Project not found — it may have been deleted.
project.loadError: Failed to load the project. Check your connection and retry.
project.readOnlyOwner: You are viewing as an observer (owner). Editing is available to the lead PM of this project.
project.autosaveBlocked: Not saved: start is after finish
project.versionFixed: Version {{v}} fixed — the next edit starts a new one
project.observersHint: An observer sees the whole project but cannot change anything.
project.subprojectsHint: The manager of this project sees and edits every subproject, and their managers see each other and the overall project. There is only one level: a subproject cannot have subprojects of its own.
project.subprojectsEmptyTab: No subprojects yet. Link existing projects from the “More” menu → “Subprojects”, and their combined picture will appear here: progress, overdue work, risks and budget for each.
project.subprojectNoCandidates: No suitable projects: only a standalone project without subprojects of its own can become a subproject.
project.archiveConfirmUmbrella: Archive this project? It will disappear from the portfolio. Its {{n}} subproject(s) are not affected — they stay in the portfolio on their own.
project.deleteConfirmUmbrella: Delete project «{{name}}»? This cannot be undone. Its {{n}} subproject(s) will NOT be deleted — they become standalone projects.
project.createAsSubproject: The new project will become a subproject of: {{parent}}
project.subprojectAttachFailed: The project was created, but linking it to the umbrella failed — do it from «More» → «Subprojects».
project.transferKeepsAccess: You stay on as a co-manager: the project remains accessible to you, but the person you pick becomes its owner and sees it among their projects.

hints.full_name: Full name of the team member. Example: John Smith — Lead Developer
hints.position: Official job title in the company. Example: Senior Software Engineer, Dept. Manager
hints.project_role: Specific role assigned within this project. Example: Backend Lead, QA Coordinator, Business Analyst
hints.email: Work email for project notifications and task assignments
hints.phone: Contact phone number for urgent project matters

guide.s1d: Click "Add member": the directory suggests names, and you can create a new person right there.
guide.s2d: Fill in position and project role — it's instantly clear who owns what.
guide.s3d: Add email and phone — handy for notifications and quick contact.
guide.s4d: Click a cell to edit it; drag the grip on the left to reorder rows.
guide.s5d: Excel export lives in the "More" menu; open a member's change history via the message icon.

hints.name: Full name of the stakeholder. Example: Maria Ivanova — IT Department Director
hints.role: Organizational role or position. Example: Sponsor, Department Head, End User Representative
hints.type: Internal = within your organization. External = client, vendor, regulator, partner
hints.influence: How much power they have over the project (1=minimal, 10=can stop the project). Score 1-10
hints.interest: How much they care about the project outcome (1=indifferent, 10=daily involvement). Score 1-10
hints.engagementStrategy: How you plan to work with this person. Example: Weekly status email, Invite to steering committee
hints.email: Email address for formal communications and invitations
hints.notes: Additional context: preferences, concerns, history. Example: Prefers brief updates, concerned about timeline

guide.s1d: Click "Add Stakeholder" and list everyone who influences or is affected by the project
guide.s2d: Set internal/external and rate influence and interest 1–10 — the quadrant is computed for you
guide.s3d: The matrix appears once both scores are set; the green quadrant needs the most attention
guide.s4d: In the "Engagement Strategy" column note how and how often you engage each person
guide.s5d: Influence and interest change — update scores; Excel export is in the project header menu

guideDefinitions.engagementStrategyDesc: The practical way you work with this person: what updates they get, how often, and how actively you involve them.
guideDefinitions.manageCloselyDesc: High influence and high interest. Involve them often in key decisions and keep them very close to the project.
guideDefinitions.keepSatisfiedDesc: High influence but lower day-to-day interest. Give clear executive-level updates without overwhelming detail.
guideDefinitions.keepInformedDesc: High interest but lower influence. Keep them updated so support and trust stay strong.
guideDefinitions.monitorDesc: Low influence and low interest. Check in periodically in case their position changes.

hints.type: Assumption = something you believe to be true but haven't confirmed. Constraint = a fixed limitation. Dependency = reliance on an external factor
hints.description: Describe the assumption, constraint or dependency clearly. Example: 'The client will provide test data by March 1'
hints.owner: Person responsible for tracking and validating this item. Example: Project Manager, Business Analyst
hints.status: Active = needs monitoring. Confirmed = validated as true. Invalid = turned out to be wrong

guide.s1d: Click Add and capture every assumption, constraint, and external dependency of the project
guide.s2d: Set the type: Assumption, Constraint, or Dependency — it shows what you can and cannot control
guide.s3d: Click the Owner cell and pick the team member responsible for tracking the item
guide.s4d: Edit any cell with a click; record check results in the item history (chat icon)
guide.s5d: Confirmed when verified, Invalid when disproven — then revisit the plan and the risks

guideDefinitions.assumptionDesc: Something the team currently believes is true and is using for planning until it is verified.
guideDefinitions.constraintDesc: A hard project limit such as budget, deadline, capacity, technology, or policy.
guideDefinitions.dependencyDesc: External work or a condition your project relies on but does not fully control.
guideDefinitions.statusesDesc: Active = still relevant. Confirmed = checked and still true. Invalid = disproven and the plan must be adjusted.

hints.goal: Purpose of this communication. Example: 'Align on sprint priorities', 'Report project health to sponsor'
hints.audience: Target audience or stakeholder group. Example: Steering Committee, Development Team, End Users
hints.topic: What information will be communicated. Example: Budget status, Risk review, Sprint demo
hints.channel: Communication medium. Example: Email, Teams meeting, In-person, Confluence page, Slack channel
hints.frequency: How often this communication happens. Example: Weekly, Bi-weekly, Monthly, On milestone completion
hints.responsible: Person who prepares and sends this communication. Example: PM, Team Lead, Analyst

guide.s1d: Click "Add Item" and enter the goal — why this communication exists (the only required field)
guide.s2d: Who you report to and where: email, meeting, chat — see the column hints for examples
guide.s3d: Monthly for sponsors, weekly for the team — a steady rhythm kills the "any news?" questions
guide.s4d: Click the cell and pick a person from the directory — every item gets exactly one owner
guide.s5d: Edit cells with a click, drag rows to reorder, discuss an item in its history — the chat icon

hints.name: Clear measurable goal for the project. Example: 'Reduce order processing time from 5 days to 2 days'
hints.status: On Track = progressing as planned. At Risk = might miss target. Off Track = already behind
hints.formula: How this KPI is measured. Example: 'Avg processing time = sum(completion_date - order_date) / count(orders)'
hints.description: Additional context about the KPI. Example: 'Measured monthly using production system data'
hints.target: The value you are aiming for. Without it a metric status is an opinion, not a measurement.
hints.unit: Unit of measure: %, pcs, days, EUR.

guide.s1d: 3–5 measurable outcomes — talk about project success in numbers, not gut feeling
guide.s2d: Click “Add KPI”; edit goal, description and formula right in the cell
guide.s3d: Write down how each metric is calculated so anyone can verify it
guide.s4d: Each reporting period click the status; keep progress notes in the history (chat icon)
guide.s5d: At Risk or Off Track — plan actions; export the table via the header menu → Excel

guideDefinitions.onTrackDesc: The metric is going to plan — normal monitoring is enough, no action needed.
guideDefinitions.atRiskDesc: Early warning signs — act now, before the KPI slips into the red zone.
guideDefinitions.offTrackDesc: The metric is already missing the target — escalate and treat it as a problem.
guideDefinitions.formulaDesc: A short note on how the KPI is calculated so everyone measures it the same way.

wbs.title: Work Breakdown Structure
wbs.noTasks: No tasks yet. Add the first task.
wbs.deleteConfirm: Delete this task and all its subtasks?

hints.title: Task name — short and action-oriented. Example: 'Design database schema', 'Prepare test scenarios'
hints.task_type: Phase = group of tasks. Task = concrete work item. Milestone = key checkpoint with no duration
hints.status: Current state: Not started → In progress → Completed. Use On hold if blocked, Cancelled if dropped
hints.priority: Critical = blocks others. High = important for deadline. Medium = standard. Low = can be deferred
hints.assignee_name: Person doing this work. Pick from People Directory or type freely
hints.planned_start: When work should begin. Format: dd.mm.yyyy
hints.planned_end: When work should be completed. Auto-calculates duration from start date
hints.actual_start: When work actually started — fill in when the person begins working
hints.duration_days: Number of working days. Auto-calculated from start-end, or type manually to set end date
hints.progress: Completion percentage 0-100%. Update regularly to track progress on Gantt chart
hints.description: Additional details, acceptance criteria, or notes for the assignee
hints.condition: Auto-calculated status alert: Overdue, Should Start, Late Start, Stalled, etc.
hints.co_assignees: Who else works on this. One person owns the task — that is the «Assignee» column.

guide.s1d: Use the Phase button to split the project into major stages, initiation to rollout
guide.s2d: Break each phase into 1–10 day tasks. The Bulk button creates a whole list at once
guide.s3d: Click a cell to type planned dates. Set dependencies in the task card (pencil icon)
guide.s4d: One owner per task. Send the task to Bitrix24 straight from its row
guide.s5d: Update % and actual dates. The Condition column flags overdue and stalled work

wbs.densityHint: Compact rows: more tasks fit on screen
wbs.coAssigneesHint: One person still owns the task. Co-assignees will see it in My tasks.
wbs.descriptionInCard: The description is edited in the card — click to open it

followups.title: All action items
followups.empty: Action items from all meetings in one list — nothing gets lost
followups.emptyOpen: No open action items — everything is done
followups.meetingsEmptyValue: Agenda, decisions and action items of every meeting — in one place. Nothing gets lost.
followups.taskCreated: The action item became a plan task
followups.finalLocked: The meeting is finalized — the action item status cannot be changed

gantt.title: Gantt Chart
gantt.emptyState: No tasks yet. Add tasks in WBS first, or create one here.

guide.s1d: Gantt reads tasks from the WBS: add phases, tasks and dates there — or create a task right here
guide.s2d: Drag a bar or its right edge — dependent tasks shift automatically. Phases can't be dragged
guide.s3d: Draw a link with the mouse from one bar to another. The critical path is outlined in red
guide.s4d: Today line, grey baseline bars and % inside bars. Double-click a task to open its card

gantt.phaseLocked: A phase's dates are derived from its tasks — move the tasks inside the phase.
gantt.criticalPathHint: The chain of tasks that drives the whole project deadline: delaying any of them moves the finish. Such bars are outlined red.
gantt.baselineHint: The grey bar under a task shows the planned dates from a saved snapshot (“Baseline”) — how far the task drifted from what was promised.
gantt.todayHint: The red vertical line is today's date. Everything to its left should be done.

baseline.title: Baseline
baseline.name: Baseline Name
baseline.selectToCompare: Select a baseline to compare with current plan

guide.s1d: A snapshot captures planned task dates — check they are filled in the WBS
guide.s2d: Click “Save Baseline” — the name “Plan as of date” is pre-filled for you
guide.s3d: Dates shift, the snapshot keeps the promised ones — grey bars on the Gantt show it
guide.s4d: The latest snapshot opens right away; pick the current plan or another one in “Compare with”
guide.s5d: Red = slipped over 7 days; chips filter tasks overdue now and tasks whose plan changed

baseline.compareHintTwo: Comparing two snapshots: left — “{{a}}”, right — “{{b}}” (by planned dates).
baseline.compareHintNeedTwo: The snapshot is compared to the current plan. To compare two plans, save one more snapshot with “Save baseline”.
baseline.compareHintPick: The snapshot is compared to the current plan. Pick another snapshot in “Compare with” to compare two plans.

hints.code: Auto-generated risk identifier. Example: R-001, R-002
hints.titleCol: Short risk name. Example: 'Key developer leaves', 'Server capacity exceeded'
hints.description: Detailed risk description: what could go wrong and under what conditions
hints.probability: Likelihood of occurrence: Low (1) = unlikely, Medium (2) = possible, High (3) = very likely
hints.impact: Consequences if the risk occurs: Low (1) = minor delay, Medium (2) = significant, High (3) = project failure
hints.score: Auto-calculated: Probability × Impact. 7-9 = critical (red), 4-6 = moderate (yellow), 1-3 = low (green)
hints.status: Open = being monitored. Mitigated = reduced. Accepted = acknowledged, no action. Closed = no longer relevant. Occurred = happened
hints.category: Technical, Financial, Operational, External, or Personnel — helps group and analyze risks
hints.owner: Person responsible for monitoring this risk and executing the response plan
hints.mitigation: What you will DO to prevent or reduce this risk. Example: 'Cross-train team members on key skills'
hints.contingencyPlan: What to do IF the risk occurs. Example: 'Engage contractor for 2 weeks to cover the gap'

guide.s1d: Click Add Risk and note everything that could go wrong — the R-NN code is assigned automatically.
guide.s2d: Pick probability and impact — the Score is computed for you and the risk lands on the 3×3 matrix.
guide.s3d: Check the Action column, then fill in the Mitigation and Contingency plans.
guide.s4d: Give every risk one owner who watches it and triggers the response plan in time.
guide.s5d: Update statuses at every status meeting and log progress via the comment icon on the row.

guideDefinitions.probabilityImpactDesc: Probability is how likely the risk is to happen. Impact is how hard it would hit time, budget, and quality.
guideDefinitions.actionDesc: An automatic cue based on the score: 6–9 avoid, 3–4 mitigate, 1–2 accept. A hint, not an order.
guideDefinitions.openDesc: The risk is live: monitor it, prepare the response plan, and keep the history updated.
guideDefinitions.closedDesc: The risk is no longer relevant, consciously accepted, or has already happened and is managed as an issue.

hints.what: Clear statement of what was decided. Example: 'Use PostgreSQL instead of MongoDB for the main database'
hints.description: Context and details about the decision
hints.why: Reasoning behind the decision. Example: 'PostgreSQL offers better transaction support for our financial data'
hints.status: Active — the decision stands. Superseded — replaced by a newer one. Revoked — the decision was cancelled.
hints.decidedBy: Person or group who made the decision. Example: Steering Committee, CTO, Project Manager
hints.madeAt: Date when the decision was made
hints.impact: What this decision affects. Example: 'Changes database technology stack, requires team retraining'
hints.alternatives: Other options that were considered. Example: 'MongoDB — rejected due to weak transaction support'

guide.s1d: Picked an approach, tech, or priority? Add a row — code D-NN is assigned automatically
guide.s2d: Title, Decided by, and Rationale settle future arguments about who decided and why
guide.s3d: Rejected options and Impact show what the decision cost when it comes up for review
guide.s4d: Decisions from a finalized meeting land in the log automatically — just review them here
guide.s5d: Mark Superseded or Revoked instead of deleting; discuss in the row's comments

budget.title: Budget
budget.monthlyViewNote: Showing {{year}}. Edit monthly values via budget item details.

hints.category: Budget category. Example: Equipment, Labour, Materials, Contractors, Travel, Licenses
hints.itemName: Specific budget line item. Example: 'Cloud hosting (AWS)', 'QA Engineer contract'
hints.description: Details about this budget item. Example: '3 months × €2000/month for AWS infrastructure'
hints.forecast: Estimated total cost for this item. Enter the planned amount
hints.actual: Actual amount spent so far. Update as invoices come in
hints.variance: Auto-calculated: Forecast − Actual. Positive = under budget, Negative = over budget

guide.s1d: Name, category from the list and Planned amount — the total budget adds up from your items.
guide.s2d: Switch to Income and add revenue items — see expected income and profit at a glance.
guide.s3d: In the Monthly plan view spread the plan across months — Free shows what's left.
guide.s4d: Actuals are entered only by month and auto-sum into the item's Actual amount column.
guide.s5d: Set an Approved limit via the pencil, watch the chart and export to Excel.

budget.monthlyHint: Enter plan and actuals by month — saved automatically. Switch the year for multi-year projects.
budget.emptyIncome: Add income lines and plan revenue by month.
budget.freeHint: Line budget minus the monthly plan already allocated (across all years)
budget.factFromMonthly: Actuals are entered by month and summed automatically
budget.rateHint: Hours turn into money at the moment you enter them — changing the rate does not recalculate past months.
budget.consolidatedHint: The block plans are yours; what has been spent is pulled from the subprojects that attributed their items to a block. The remainder of a block is what you can still commission.
budget.fromUmbrella: Taken from the parent project's budget
budget.fromUmbrellaHint: Blocks of «{{name}}»: how much the block holds, how much every subproject has already spent from it, and how much of that is yours.
budget.noBlocks: The parent project has no expense blocks yet.
budget.noBlocksOwn: No expense blocks yet — add budget items and subprojects will be able to attribute their spending to them.
budget.orphans: Some spending is attributed to blocks that no longer exist ({{sum}}): {{list}}. Re-attribute it or restore the block.
budget.mixedCurrencies: The tree mixes currencies ({{list}}). The portal does not convert, so block totals only count projects using the parent project's currency.
budget.attribute: Attribute spending to the parent project's blocks
budget.attributeHint: Your amounts stay yours — attributing merely shows the manager of «{{name}}» which block this spending comes from.
budget.fromHoursHint: Worked out from hours at the rate — type an amount to set it by hand

backlog.title: Backlog
backlog.promoteConfirm: Promote this item to the WBS plan? A new task will be created.

hints.titleField: Short description of the request. Example: 'Add export to PDF feature'
hints.description: Full description with context, user story, or acceptance criteria
hints.priority: Critical = urgent blocker. High = needed for next release. Medium = planned. Low = nice-to-have
hints.status: New — just added. In review — being discussed. Approved — ready to move to WBS. Rejected — will not be done. Promoted — a task was created from it. In progress, Done and Cancelled come from Bitrix24 via the linked task.
hints.estimatedDays: Rough estimate in days. Example: 3 = about 3 working days of effort
hints.requestedBy: Who asked for this. Example: Client, Product Owner, Team Member
hints.plannedStart: Planned start date. With days or end filled, the other is computed automatically.
hints.plannedEnd: Planned end date. Recomputed from start and days (and vice versa).
hints.assignee: Task assignee. Carried to Bitrix and when promoting to the work plan.

guide.s1d: Ideas and requests go here; action items from finalized meetings arrive automatically as B-NN
guide.s2d: Edit dates, priority and status right in the table; the full description and the other fields live in the card: click the item code or the pencil next to the title.
guide.s3d: Rank items by business value and urgency: from Critical down to Low
guide.s4d: The arrow in the row creates a real WBS task — the item leaves the backlog
guide.s5d: Filter by status and reject what you won't do — the backlog stays an honest list
